back: Two towers (image encoder, text encoder), each projected to the same $d$ and L2-normalised; similarity is cosine.

front: Gradient of the CLIP loss w.r.t. logits

back: Learned scalar (initialised at 0.07, parametrised in log space and clipped). Small: sharp, hard-negative focus; large: flat. Argmax at inference is unaffected.
$\log N$ when all logits in a row are equal (an $N$-way guess).
$N-1$ negatives per pair; more negatives give a stronger learning signal (CLIP used batch sizes around 32k).
Per-pair sigmoid binary loss $\log(1+e^{-y_{ij}S_{ij}})$ with $y=+1$ on the diagonal, $-1$ elsewhere; no softmax normalisation, no all-gather.
Prompts (a photo of a {class}) -> text embeddings $T$; image embedding $u$; predict $\arg\max_c T_c\cdot u$ after normalising.
Average the embeddings of several templates per class, then re-normalise; typically a small gain.
Rank by cosine similarity; recall@k = fraction of queries whose correct item is in the top $k$.

front: Zero-shot vs linear probe vs fine-tune
back: Zero-shot: no training. Probe: usually better in-domain. Fine-tune: best in-domain but may hurt zero-shot transfer.
Dependence on web data and its biases, prompt sensitivity, weak at fine-grained/spatial/counting, uncalibrated similarities, one global vector per image.
Zero-shot classification, retrieval, open-vocabulary detection/segmentation, vision encoder of multimodal LLMs, text conditioning for image generation.
Positives span two modalities, so the $N\times N$ matrix needs no diagonal masking and is cross-entropied in both directions; negatives are the other $N-1$ items.
